i: Labour cost high (reported ~40%); needs materially higher weekly sales to bring labour toward ~30% — Owner: GM (TBC) / HC (from Shoreditch project mtg 22/07/2026)
Difficulty reducing BOH labour hours while keeping operations stable -> more cross-training between sushi and FOH needed — Owner: HC/GM (22/07/2026)
KPI-sheet reporting error on the labour-cost entry identified and corrected — Owner: Kaitlin (22/07/2026)
Cluster directive (aligned): when replacing departing staff, hire regular FOH rather than AGMs to optimise labour cost — Owner: GMs (21/07/2026)
Cluster directive (aligned): reduce labour via earlier closing procedures and optimised shift schedules — Owner: GMs (21/07/2026)
Labour running well above the site's own target and a stock gap still open, despite covers and sales beating target.
Delivery sales fell sharply week on week and spend per head dropped, even as covers rose.
Toxic team culture — false rumours and negative talk between staff, with one team member repeatedly named as the source.
Management itself contributing: complaints about teammates and firing decisions being aired to other staff rather than handled directly.
Site manager has the willingness but not the method — ordering, stock counts and invoice recording are not on a fixed routine.
Stock management and closing procedures not being followed consistently; team training outstanding.
Deliveroo tablet downtime caused lost sales — the device was not being kept charged; a new charging setup is now in place.
Labour projections skewed by incorrect hour logging.
Site management structure unstable; routines being reset with closer supervision.
Region-wide (South England): Cleanliness standards need to be stricter across the region, with closer oversight of service consistency and brand reputation.
Region-wide (South England): Management teams have not been trained on EHO procedures.
Region-wide (South England): The B2B outreach tracker is not being maintained — leads are not colour-coded and entries carry no timestamps.
Region-wide (South England): B2B activity across the region is too low, and the DAM and AM are not copied on all partner communication.
Region-wide (South England): Summer menu changes and pest-control protocols still to be rolled out across sites.
Covers had been input per meal instead of per table, skewing spend-per-head data — now corrected, stabilising SPH at ~£23.
Delivery issues and rejected orders prompted a new rule that staff photograph all delivery packaging.
Site operating without a permanent GM and AGM — recruitment for both roles underway.
Daily food checks not reliably completed on time; alarms being introduced to enforce them.
Targets missed as the Boomtown festival pulled trade away and pushed labour up.
Labour still above target, although at its lowest point so far.
Excessive food ordering to support other sites has been stopped to stabilise food cost.
The GM / head chef meeting was deferred again.
Chinese cooker out of action for the third time.
Supervisors closing without supervision - standards slip, including windows left open.
Management structure not yet scalable beyond the current GM, AGM and supervisors.
Record Deliveroo week with very low late orders and strong compliance, with the new AGM now on the compliance system.
Sales targets are being met largely through walk ins and side sales rather than bookings.
Deliveroo prep times have increased and late prepared orders need bringing back inside the standard prep time target.
Compliance was marked down for a missed daily food check.
Several staff have had probation periods extended for not meeting efficiency standards.
Back of house staff are refusing requests to take longer breaks during the quiet early afternoon period, which needs resolving against the break policy.
Bar staff are failing to record expiry dates and wastage.
A staff member is to be trained on the bar with no prior bar experience, which risks service disruption if done at busy times.
There is concern that a single person cannot hold the floor at this site once more than a few tables are seated, as it is larger than Lakeside.
Ordering errors are occurring because orders are not always being taken on the iPad.
Administrative work is being done in guest seating areas, leaving the visible restaurant floor untidy and unprofessional.
Printed kids menus featuring the kids bento box are not available, so the family offer is not being communicated.
Delivery orders need to be prioritised alongside a busier dine-in trade.
Leslie needs further training on the payroll and onboarding trackers, and the payroll sheet is out of date for holidays and departures.
Labour is not well balanced between back of house kitchen porter duties and front of house floor support during peak service.

Region-wide (South England): Inconsistent service standards across the region were identified as the single biggest area for improvement, with basics such as checking back on tables, recommending dishes and engaging with customers not being done reliably.

Region-wide (South England): A lack of structured pre-shift planning is leaving teams short of essentials such as ice and napkins, forcing managers to scramble mid service and affecting customer satisfaction.
A very large negative drinks variance was reported but is inaccurate, caused by incorrect data entry and double counting of stock takes, and the correct figure will be entered in the coming week.
The dedicated kitchen porter role is being removed because the role was not fully utilised, with those duties passing to front of house staff from this week.
Leslie and Jada need training on management tasks, which has been scheduled with the area manager.

The Red Bull Gaming partnership activation is moving from Soho to Shoreditch from next week and includes a 15 percent discount for their groups, so a memo on the correct use of discount buttons is being issued to ensure accurate tracking.
Cover is needed for tonight's shift and Karki's availability needs to be confirmed.

Region-wide (South England): The brand weekly average review rating is trending below target and needs to improve, as a single negative review can drag the average down despite many positive ones, so consistent cleaning and service standards are needed across the region.
Region-wide (South England): A memo on the correct use of discount buttons is being issued and needs to be checked by the group for accuracy so that discounts are recorded and tracked correctly.

Region-wide (South England): Google reviews are missing from the KPI sheet and need to be added, filed region-wide because Nikki, who was given the action, could not be resolved to a site from the transcript.
Pest control has not been carried out as scheduled and the provider needs calling today; visits should be happening at least every couple of months.
Covers rose slightly and spend per head increased on heavy upselling, with sales hitting target and up on the week.
Deliveroo orders are being rejected, most likely because a till update made all steak ramen halal and removed the separate halal steak buttons from the till.
Deliveroo performance itself was clean, with no prep errors, no inaccuracies and all five star ratings.

Labour is projected above the target because the rush is a short one hour window that needs three staff through the afternoon; the target deliberately allows more cover than the leanest option because service quality and the first impression for new customers matter more.
Quiet periods should be used for cleaning compliance and staff tasks, and staff efficiency during steady shifts remains a challenge.
The drinks stock count showed a zero count alongside a large negative variance, recorded while a new head chef was being trained during a period of manager absence.
Two two star reviews came from confusion between the vegan and the vegetarian ramen; the head chef will run back of house training and CCTV was reviewed with the team member involved.
Covers rose and sales beat target, driven by large office groups and walk ins, while spend per head fell because of loyalty app ramen deals and half price offers.
Deliveroo late prep orders increased because a new back of house hire was slow on gyoza and mixed up chicken and vegetable gyoza orders; that hire is being let go after the training period.
A missing Fanta on a delivery order was identified through the photo proof on the dedicated iPad, and photo checks are now mandatory.
Labour rose because of training the new back of house hire and adding one extra person at lunch.
The wet variance ran adverse, attributed to soft drink training.
The Google rating improved after a one star review was removed.
A new front of house starter worked shifts before their right to work check had cleared, which is not permitted.
No compliance tasks were late but they were not ticked off in the compliance app, so four daily alarms have been set.
Covers rose by 82 (7.37%) week on week while spend per head fell £0.60 (2.80%), which the site puts down to the free ramen and £5 ramen offers.
Sales were up £1,053.02 (4.29%) week on week and finished £2,096.79 (8.92%) above target.
Food cost was 30.44%, driven by guests choosing seafood or steak ramen on the offers, food mistakes by new FOH staff and a lot of waste.
Deliveroo is on a red light for missed items and late preparation, and Deliveroo sales are going down.
The Google rating for the week was 5.00.
Steak tataki, Hell ramen and yuzu tom yum showed white residue, and the supplier has been queried as the cause.
Chicken karaage portions are causing waste.
Customers complained of cold curry sauce, and two tables had cold ramen on Saturday when BOH was understaffed.
Covers fell by 12 (1%) to 1,182 week on week while spend per head rose by £0.34 (1.63%) to £21.16; 103 guests came from the hotel app on Sunday between 12pm and 3pm at 15% off.
Sales were £25,586.23, down £10.57 (0.04%) week on week and £2,086.22 (8.88%) above the £23,500 target.
The report puts potential revenue at a further £4,750.06; sales are capping at around £25K and extra labour will be used to send out flyers.
SPH was held back by free ramen, £5 ramen and SLL offers, and the 50% SLL offer brings down the sales number.
Wage cost was 28.45% and food cost 27.86%; adjusted for discounts (£30,000 total sales including £4,500 of discounts against £7,280 of labour), labour is 24% rather than 28%.
Food and drinks variance was 2% (food 2.0%, wet 2.2%), and the head chef puts actual food cost at a normal 23% to 24%.
Labour notes: hiring continues, more hours are going into training, BOH could not take two hour breaks because of prep, and more FOH is needed because the site is busy.
Saturday sales have surged from around £2.7K to £4K to £5K (£4.5K last week and £4.4K the week before) because of B2B partnerships, hotel apps and app advertising.
Covers rose by 5 (0.42%) week on week and spend per head rose by £0.04 (0.18%).
Sales rose by £510.30 (2%) week on week and were £2,596.52 (11.05%) above target.
Food and drinks variance was 3.8% (food 4.3%, wet 0.4%).
Google rating for the week was 5.00, against a target of 40 five star reviews a week.
The site is still looking to hire a sushi chef, and who will lead that hire is to be confirmed; Gerry is training as part time sushi cover and the head chef will train a sushi chef this week.
A two week Deliveroo 30% off promotion starts on Monday 12/10, with Shoreditch in the first wave; whether to run a Halloween event is still open.
FOH standards are inconsistent across different managers.
BOH punctuality must follow the handbook, and at closing 10 to 15 minutes are allowed for admin, with compliance done first before cleaning starts.
Covers rose by 193 (16.25%) week on week and spend per head fell by £0.97, which the site put down to the SLL 50% discount and £5 ramen promotions, with guests ordering cheap ramen and fewer drinks.

Sales rose by £2,624.69 (10.05%) week on week and were £5,201.21 (22.22%) above target, with Thursday to Saturday getting busy; Ziang Lin called it a record week of £28,000 (up 22%) despite heavy discounting alongside SLL.
It was unclear whether the SLL promotion ended last week; Ziang Lin will check with Matt and said the discount will be reinstated if sales drop further.
Food and drinks variance was 7.3% (food 8.9%, wet minus 3.8%), an unexpected food variance jump from 3.5% to 8.9%.
Labour was 24.18%.
Google rating for the week was 5.00.

Deliveroo late prepared orders rose while prep times fell, and the Deliveroo rating dipped to 4.4 after 1 star reviews about too little katsu curry sauce, an added egg mistake, cutlery and curry portions; a yakisoba issue was also reviewed.
Chicken katsu curry was out of stock and due back on 21/10.
Matthew Alderson-Jenner reported Shoreditch sales of £25.5K last week with wages at 25.36% (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Michael Salvador said Shoreditch customers are coming back (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Labour has come down partly because the outside area is now closed as it gets colder (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Sushi chefs are cross training on cocktails and the bar and FOH staff are covering KP; the plan to move the sushi station to the food pass has not been done yet (Admin Meeting 26/10).

Many tables have purple lights instead of warm barrel lights, so the purple menu cannot be read; after complaints the site asked for table lights or ceiling lights, and Ziang Lin wants to agree with Michael Salvador whether to buy table lights or bring in an electrician (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Ziang Lin said Shoreditch competes with five big chains nearby, including Bone Daddies, Tonkotsu and Wagamama, and that the layout has made the site hard to run from the start (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Shoreditch needs a Deliveroo rider scan tag so riders scan on arrival and rider wait times are tracked accurately; Matthew Alderson-Jenner is requesting one (Admin Meeting 26/10).
Ziang Lin would run QR code ordering at Shoreditch because it is a large floor for one or two staff to cover (Admin Meeting 26/10).
